live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that opens P2 (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam weighed at oshb:Ezek.3.27 above. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) recurs the exact word from 3:25 on the far side of the parent seam, disclosed as continuity evidence the seam-assessment above already weighed. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe recorded after it, before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. This is the question the division plan holds for chs 4-7, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. Named and weighed under A9: on the near face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3, and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the far face oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: in the pinned inventory no verse of ch 4 belongs to the messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event classes, the chapter's only listed members being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is absent from both the 81-verse utterance list and the 64-verse recognition family - so CUT-RULE's second limb is not met; and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side, so its first limb is not met either. A mark alone never satisfies limb (b). The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. The test is reworded because its earlier form omitted 4:3, the very verse the mark follows: the titled sub-onset וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ stands at 4:1 and again at 5:1, whereas bare וְאַתָּ֤ה without the title opens three interior stages - 4:3, 4:4 and 4:9 - so the text stages the siege-model, the iron pan, the two lying postures and the rationed food as one commanded act and not as separate commands (oshb:Ezek.4.1).

No boundary is argued from the absent mark, only from the pe that follows and the topical restatement it closes. That near face is a verdict clause with no formula of its own -- the discourse close of the disputation, corroborated by the pe that follows and by no formula -- while the far face past it opens the next unit on the dateline at 33:21. A close seam whose near face is a discourse close without a formula is what this row's medium_low records, whatever stands on its far face.

live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: the verse opens on the hand-of-YHWH idiom immediately followed by a transport verb, oshb:Ezek.37.1 הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת -- the same onset shape that opens the book's other three long prose visions, and this occurrence is one of only 7 hand-of-YHWH verses in the book. The unit is held as one scene, with the live rival inside it weighed below: the prophet is set down among the bones (37.1-2), questioned and commanded to prophesy twice -- once to the bones, once to the breath/spirit (37.4-6, 37.9), watches the two-stage reanimation (37.7-8, 37.10), and receives the scene's own interpretation as a word to 'son of man' (oshb:Ezek.37.11 וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ). Close: oshb:Ezek.37.14 stacks three refrain-grade closes in one verse -- the second-person plural recognition variant ('and you will know that I am YHWH', part of a 21-verse 2mp family sweep), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (one of 14 book-wide), and the short utterance signature without the divine-name pair (one of only 4 such short forms in the book) -- וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and a pe mark is recorded immediately after this verse (tier-3 single-witness, informing not deciding). Both sides of the following seam were weighed: oshb:Ezek.37.15 opens with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, one of 39 verses carrying that strict form, so the close at 37.14 and the fresh onset at 37.15 corroborate each other from both directions. Both faces of that close are top grade; the row is held at medium because a licensed rival stands inside the span, at the 37.10/37.11 seam.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at the two samekh-marked points inside the scene: after the army stands up at oshb:Ezek.37.10, and after the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.37.12 (tier-3 single-witness marks on both). The first is a real and licensed rival: 37.11 opens on a he-said-to-me clause with the son-of-man address (sweep: 93 verses book-wide), a default onset inside a vision, with the samekh standing behind it on 37.10 -- so 37.1-10 would be a complete scene (the question, the command to prophesy, and the army that stands up as its result) and 37.11-14 its interpretation, which carries a messenger formula of its own at 37.12 and a recognition close. It is not taken because 37.1-14 is held as one vision_report unit; the other he-said-to-me verses inside the scene (37.3, 37.4, 37.9) are dialogue turns that leave no scene-complete piece behind them, and the transport at 37.2 would leave a one-verse remainder. That licensed rival is what holds this row at medium rather than high; which of the recognition clauses at 37.6, 37.13 and 37.14 closes the row is held open here.
live_prose.device_notes: 37.2 and 37.9 each carry one paseq (count-only, single-witness, no intra-verse position sourceable from the extract). 37.9 also carries an OSHB editorial note recording an accent divergence from BHS (single-witness apparatus, not a text variant). The WEB prints a mid-verse paragraph inside 37.3 (“Son of man, can these bones live?” (web:Ezek.37.3), then the prophet's reply) -- tier-4 texture, cited only and never a boundary argument. The witness also records a samekh after MT 36:38 (single witness), the paragraph mark behind this row's onset. The second-person plural recognition variant stands inside the scene at 37.6 as well as at the close, disclosed here and arguing no boundary.

live_prose.boundary_rationale: Onset: the strict word-event formula reopens at oshb:Ezek.37.15 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, following the pe mark recorded after oshb:Ezek.37.14 (behind this row, tier-3 single-witness, closing the unit before it) and followed at 37.16 by the commanded symbolic action (“You, son of man, take one stick” (web:Ezek.37.16)). The row runs as one unbroken masoretic paragraph internally, framed only by the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28, so the tradition itself treats the demonstration (37.16-20) and its spoken interpretation (37.21-28, opened by a messenger formula with no addressee change) as a single section. Close: oshb:Ezek.37.28 carries a wide-family recognition close addressed to 'the nations' rather than the strict third-person plural (this expansion sits in the wider 64-verse recognition sweep, not the strict 28-verse list) -- וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בִּהְי֧וֹת מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם -- with a samekh mark recorded immediately after. Both sides were weighed: the onset word-event at 37.15 is one of only 39 strict-form verses in the book, corroborated behind it by the pe at 37.14, and the samekh-marked recognition close at 37.28 is corroborated from the close side before the next word-event opens the following unit at oshb:Ezek.38.1.
live_prose.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split between the stick demonstration and its interpretation, e.g. after web:Ezek.37.20 (“The sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes.” (web:Ezek.37.20)) or after web:Ezek.37.23 (the purification promise). Rejected: reading each section mark as standing on the verse it follows, no samekh or pe falls in this row's INTERIOR, oshb:Ezek.37.15-Ezek.37.27 (single-witness; the only marks anywhere in range are the pe recorded on 37.14, behind the onset seam, and the samekh recorded on 37.28, at the close seam), and the messenger-formula reopenings at oshb:Ezek.37.19 and oshb:Ezek.37.21 do not change addressee, so neither meets the addressee-change condition required before a messenger formula is read as a row seam.
live_prose.device_notes: Operative-category disclosure: the 37.15-28 span is anchored as sign_act (the commanded stick action of 37.16-20), but its interpretation at 37.21-28 carries the salvation_oracle burden (gather/return, the covenant of peace at 37.26, ‘my servant David’ and ‘my sanctuary’ devices) -- a one-clause category deviation rather than a split: the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28 are the row's only framing marks, and the addressee stays constant across both halves. 37.16 is a doubled ketiv/qere verse: two notes on one verse, each written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.16, ketiv), and each read as the same consonantal word under different pointing -- the first note reads חֲבֵרָ֑יו and the second חֲבֵרָֽיו, the two differing by exactly one codepoint, U+0591 HEBREW ACCENT ETNAHTA in the first against U+05BD HEBREW POINT METEG in the second (MEASURED by diffing the two members of the kq entry at this verse in the section-mark record, codepoint by codepoint; WLC/OSHB, single witness), and 37.19 carries one further note on the same word (written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, ketiv), read חֲבֵרָ֑יו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, Qere)); 37.22 carries a further K/Q note in this span (written יהיה (oshb:Ezek.37.22, ketiv), read יִֽהְיוּ (oshb:Ezek.37.22, Qere)). A boundary is never argued from any of these Qere readings; they are disclosed as textual-variant sites only.

A transport verb sits inside this row at 40:24, וַיּוֹלִכֵ֨נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם (oshb:Ezek.40.24) “he led me toward the south” (web:Ezek.40.24), moving from the north gate to the south gate within the same outer court; it is disclosed as intra-row sub-onset texture, not the row seam, because it changes compass direction but not court. Close side: 40:27 ends the south outer gate on its hundred-cubit span to the inner court's south gate, וַיָּ֨מָד מִשַּׁ֧עַר אֶל הַשַּׁ֛עַר דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַדָּר֖וֹם מֵאָ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת (oshb:Ezek.40.27), immediately before 40:28's court-change transport verb. The seam at 40:27/40:28 turns on a location change -- the next verse's transport verb crosses from the outer court into the inner court -- unlike the compass-direction transport at 40:24 inside this row.
